children: Hero Motors anchors raise Rs 299.99 crore; IPO price band Rs 79–84, fresh issue Rs 600 crore, OFS Rs 400 crore; listing on NSE and BSE

Hero Motors Limited, an automotive technology company that designs and delivers powertrain solutions for OEMs in the United States, Europe, India, and the ASEAN region, has raised Rs 299.99 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering. The company allocated 3,57,14,284 equity shares at Rs 84 per share to anchor investors.

Marquee institutions participated, including ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited, 3P India Equity Fund 1million, Edelweiss Life Insurance Company Limited, Societe Generale – ODI, and ASAS Global Fund Incorporated VCC Sub Fund, among others.

Equity-oriented schemes included ICICI Prudential Smallcap Fund, Kotak Mahindra Trustee Co Ltd A/C Kotak MNC Fund and JM Financial Mutual Fund – JM Flexi Cap Fund, among others. Of the total allocation, Rs 29.164 crore equity shares were allocated to seven domestic mutual funds through 16 schemes.
ICICI Securities Limited, DAM Capital Advisors Limited, and JM Financial Limited are the book-running lead managers, with KFin Technologies Limited as registrar.

Shares are proposed to be listed on the NSE and BSE Limited. The price band for the maiden issue is Rs 79 to Rs 84 per equity share of face value Rs 10 each. The IPO will open on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, and close on Friday, September 18, 2026.

The IPO is a combination of a fresh issue of up to Rs 600 crore and an offer-for-sale of equity shares up to Rs 400 crore by promoters O P Munjal Holdings and Hero Cycles Limited. Fresh issue proceeds amount to Rs 190 crore, planned for debt repayment in full or part, expansion capex of up to Rs 200 crore for capacity enhancements at the Gautam Buddha Nagar facility, funding inorganic growth, and other corporate purposes.

The offer is being conducted through a book-building process under SEBI ICDR Regulations, with not more than 50 per cent of the net offer to QIBs, not less than 15 per cent to NIIs, and not less than 35 per cent to RIIs. The company is a leading automotive technology provider with a fully integrated powertrain portfolio, serving global customers including BMW and Ducati, among others, and is positioned for growth in both electric and non-electric powertrains.
